name: Quality Systems for AI Devices
blurb: How device quality management changes for AI.
title: Quality Systems for AI Devices
answer: AI devices run on the same quality system as other devices, now aligned with ISO 13485 in the United States since the FDA's Quality Management System Regulation took effect on 2 February 2026. AI adds data management, model training records and change control for retraining to that system.

reading.body:
AI devices do not get a separate quality system. They run on the existing device system, now aligned with ISO 13485 in the United States since the FDA's Quality Management System Regulation took effect on 2 February 2026.

What changes is the record set. Training data becomes a controlled design input with its own records, the same as specifications. Model training records and change control for retraining join the system alongside it. The regulated object is no longer only the shipped device but the data and process that produced its behavior.

This matters because retraining is the normal state of an AI device, not an exception. A conventional device is validated once and changed deliberately. A model can drift as data, labels, or upstream models change, so the quality system has to hold the link between a given dataset and a given device version. That is a documentation and traceability burden, and it lands on the same teams already carrying the device file.

The data covers one jurisdiction and one effective date. It does not say how regulators will treat continuous learning, what evidence a retraining change requires, or how any of this interacts with European requirements. It also says nothing about compute, so no claim about infrastructure follows from it.

sections.body: Treat training data as a controlled design input with its own records, the same as specifications.
